## Formula layer gates

These examples run with the formula scanner excluded, as the cmark gate runs
the base layer against its oracle. They are a harness-internal proof that a
registered feature can be excluded for a comparison, and nothing more: the
dialect has no switch, so no consumer can ask for this parse. In that layer
every formula syntax is ordinary Markdown.

```````````````````````````````` example
Inline $x+y$ end.
.
Document scope=1:1..1:17 children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:17 children=1
    └── Text scope=1:1..1:17 literal="Inline $x+y$ end." children=0
````````````````````````````````

```````````````````````````````` example
$$
x+y
$$
.
Document scope=1:1..3:2 children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..3:2 children=5
    ├── Text scope=1:1..1:2 literal="$$" children=0
    ├── SoftBreak scope=1:3..1:3 children=0
    ├── Text scope=2:1..2:3 literal="x+y" children=0
    ├── SoftBreak scope=2:4..2:4 children=0
    └── Text scope=3:1..3:2 literal="$$" children=0
````````````````````````````````

```````````````````````````````` example
Inline \\(x+y\\) and \(a+b\).
.
Document scope=1:1..1:29 children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:29 children=1
    └── Text scope=1:1..1:29 literal="Inline \\(x+y\\) and (a+b)." children=0
````````````````````````````````

```````````````````````````````` example
Display \\[x+y\\] and \[a+b\].
.
Document scope=1:1..1:30 children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:30 children=1
    └── Text scope=1:1..1:30 literal="Display \\[x+y\\] and [a+b]." children=0
````````````````````````````````

Formula fenced-code blocks remain ordinary code when formulas are disabled.

```````````````````````````````` example
```formula
x+y
```
.
Document scope=1:1..3:3 children=1
└── CodeBlock scope=1:1..3:3 info="formula" language="formula" literal="x+y\n" fenced=true closed=true children=0
````````````````````````````````
